correctness.rationale: For any a<b with separation Δ, only cost atoms c<Δ participate and left/right turnout masses are sums w V((a+b-c)/2) and w[1-V((a+b+c)/2)], respectively. At positive turnout, moving the left candidate slightly toward the right preserves the finite active-cost set but strictly increases each V term, disproving any active pure equilibrium for strictly increasing V. Zero-turnout profiles are equilibria exactly when each opponent location lies in I_c*=[0,1]∩[1-c*,c*], else an endpoint deviation generates positive votes. Thus PNE=I_c*², with correct c*<1/2, =1/2, >1/2, >=1 boundaries. The empirical uniform m-grid costs have Kolmogorov error 1/(m+1), whence candidate payoffs differ uniformly by at most that amount. Integrating the limiting uniform game confirms quartile best responses, and the two-sided perturbation bound yields 2/(m+1)-equilibria. Independent exact checks reproduced cdf discrepancies for m=2,3,5,10,100; infinite distribution argument rests on the proof.
